findings: v009 is rejected as a visual baseline; it may be used only as negative evidence for what the v010 route must avoid.
visual_source_of_truth_v010 locks every new sprite generation to the approved model sheet plus visual DNA and direction briefs; v009/v010 sprite sheets are comparison/runtime evidence only.

The accepted identity comes from v008 as art direction only: bronze skin, aggressive hair and face, black/gold shorts, dirty white wraps, red biceps band on the non-lava arm, and a rock/lava arm with readable hand endpoint.
The v010 route must preserve character charisma before technical cell compliance. A PNG can pass PLTE, index 0 and grid checks while still failing this gate.
If v008 internal cohesion drift is confirmed, especially hair drift in the first pose, production must create a corrected model sheet brief before any sprite sheet or runtime strip.
The art target is native Mega Drive pixel art with hard 1 px structure, material-coded clusters, clean silhouette and readable face/eyes at 320x224.

game_design_context.gameplay_role: Playable close-combat Muay Thai hybrid fighter. The character reads as the player avatar in side-view combat, using disciplined guard, short forward pressure, jab, knee, teep and block while the lava arm functions as the signature visual/gameplay signal.
interaction_context: Camera is 320x224 side view, close enough for face and hand identity but wide enough for two fighters, HUD and attack reach.
Target scale remains a 48x64 cell only if the scale contract preserves visible body, hands, feet, hair and lava arm without clipping; default pivot is bottom-center at 24,58 and ground_y is 58.
Opponent is frontal on the same ground plane, usually one to two character widths away; attacks must communicate startup, reach, active contact and recovery before FX.

Hitbox/hurtbox policy: torso and head keep stable mass; jab extends the human wrapped fist, knee compresses then drives upward, teep extends the front leg while the lava hand stays visible above or beside the leg.
Scenario must support readability, not compete with the fighter. Background contrast, texture and saturation stay subordinate to outline, hair, eyes, bandages, shorts and lava cracks.
Contact policy: planted foot and root foot must be legible on ground_y during idle, walk, guard, jab and knee. Teep may lift one foot but must show the support foot and recovery path.
Runtime FX policy: hit sparks, lava bursts, glow flares, dust and impact flashes are separate runtime FX assets when used; they are not baked into the character body sheet.
Required movement states for v010 planning: front, back, guard, knee, teep or attack key pose, idle, walk_step, guard_block, jab, knee, teep, hurt and transition/recovery rules.

must_preserve.expected: Thick aggressive dark hair with consistent volume between poses; variation only by camera angle, occlusion or action force.
must_preserve.observed: v008 is the identity source but the first-pose hair drift remains an audit target before sprite production.

must_preserve.expected: Focused high-contrast eyes aimed at the opponent, with brows/eye line supporting aggression at native scale.
must_preserve.observed: v009 lost face/eye charisma; v010 must restore it through posture, contrast and a deliberate eye cluster.

must_preserve.expected: Readable fighter face: calm focus in idle/guard, jaw tension or kiai on active strikes, pain direction on hurt.
must_preserve.observed: Face acting is part of gameplay readability, not optional microdetail.

must_preserve.expected: Athletic Muay Thai body with consistent head, torso, shoulder, hip, hand and foot scale across front, back and action poses.
must_preserve.observed: No extra limbs, no amorphous endpoints, no block-mass simplification.

must_preserve.expected: Asymmetric rock/lava arm with dark stone volume, orange/yellow fissures, readable elbow/wrist/hand endpoint and no wrap or glove.
must_preserve.observed: This is the primary signature feature and cannot collapse into a gray block or generic glove.

must_preserve.expected: Glowing lava fissures read as internal heat cracks on the special arm, using hot slots and controlled cluster shapes.
must_preserve.observed: Fissures must survive palette planning without becoming noise, spray or baked FX.

must_preserve.expected: Black Muay Thai shorts with gold trim/ornament, readable as cloth and not as a single dark block.
must_preserve.observed: Shorts and trim must remain visible in key poses and 48x64 sprite planning.

must_preserve.expected: Red band on the non-lava arm biceps, consistent by side and omitted only when physically occluded by pose.
must_preserve.observed: Side-specific accessory drift was a known prior failure and is locked for v010.

must_preserve.expected: Dirty white bandages/wraps on the human hand and feet, never on the lava arm.
must_preserve.observed: Wrap placement must distinguish human limb from lava limb at native scale.

must_preserve.expected: Bronze/dark warm skin with hue-shifted shadow and enough separation from stone, cloth and wraps.
must_preserve.observed: Skin cannot be washed into the same gray/dark mass as shorts or rock.

must_preserve.expected: Palette separates outline, hair, skin, shorts, gold, dirty wraps, stone and lava cracks by function under a 16-color character domain unless FX are separated.
must_preserve.observed: Palette syntax alone is insufficient; material semantics must be visible.

must_preserve.expected: Gold trim, waistband/short markings and any emblem-like ornament stay consistent with v008 design and do not drift between poses.
must_preserve.observed: If a marking is simplified for 48x64, the simplification must preserve placement and role.

must_preserve.expected: Visible scars, crack marks or scar-like lava fissures from the approved direction must not be invented, dropped or moved without pose justification.
must_preserve.observed: The lava fissures are treated as a scar-like identity marker for continuity.

must_preserve.expected: Lava arm side, human-arm marker, wraps and body-side relationships remain coherent across front, back and action poses.
must_preserve.observed: Horizontal flip is a runtime direction tool, not permission to swap the character identity.

must_preserve.expected: Biceps band, hand wraps, foot wraps, shorts trim and any waist details stay in the same visual language and side logic.
must_preserve.observed: Accessories are identity markers and cannot become random decorative noise.

must_preserve.expected: The fighter remains recognizable in pure black silhouette: hair, guard, shorts, Muay Thai stance and lava-arm mass must be readable.
must_preserve.observed: Silhouette must pass before color blocking, sprite strips or runtime promotion.

secondary_motion: Hair reacts after torso motion with 1-2 frame delay; it compresses in guard/knee and trails in jab/teep recovery without changing identity.
Shorts, waist trim, red band and wraps move as cloth clusters with delayed settle; they cannot freeze during attacks or turn into unrelated shapes.
Breathing is visible in idle through chest/shoulder/guard micro-poses and shading shifts, not through subpixel movement or blur.
Weight is rooted in the feet: stance stays heavy, knee rises from compression, teep shows support foot and jab pays recovery.
Lava-arm cracks keep material continuity through motion; glow/impact bursts are separated as runtime FX when needed.
expression_requirements: Idle: focused closed-mouth stare aimed at the opponent.
Walk_step: focused eyes with slight jaw/shoulder tension.
Guard_block: protected face still reads aggressive, not blank.
Jab/knee/teep active frames: tightened jaw, kiai mouth or teeth indication where the face scale permits.
Hurt: visible force direction, head reaction and pain asymmetry without losing scale or identity.
state_fantasy_checks: Every state must read as a Muay Thai hybrid fighter, not a generic martial-arts mannequin.
Attacks require anticipation, active contact, hitstop-readable peak and recovery; no attack may start directly on the active frame.
The lava arm is a visual signature and gameplay signal even in states where the human arm or leg performs the strike.
Reach and contact must be clear enough for fair hitbox interpretation against a frontal opponent.
Sprite planning must preserve ground_y, pivot and frame envelope before any full sheet assembly.
